title: Childhood Confidence, Schooling, and the Labor Market: Evidence from the PSID
Got Beef with Beef? Evidence from a Large-Scale Carbon Labeling Experiment
abstract: Carbon-footprint labeling has emerged as a prominent tool to shift consumers towards lower-emissions choices, but its effectiveness remains unclear, especially in polarized settings like the US. We report on the first large-scale evaluation of carbon labeling—a randomized field experiment with over 230,000 customers of a major food company. Carbon-footprint labels reduced average emissions by only 0.6%, and they backfired among customers opposed to environmental nudges, who increased their dietary emissions. Despite limited environmental impact, the labels had positive financial returns for our partner company, increasing customer retention by 1.0% and average customer-week profits by 0.9%. Thus, while climate labels will likely remain a popular sustainability nudge, they have only small environmental benefits and may backfire in polarized settings.
abstract_zh: 碳足迹标签已成为引导消费者选择低排放产品的重要工具，但其有效性仍不明确，在美国这样的两极分化环境中尤其如此。我们报告了对碳标签的首次大规模评估——这是一项与一家大型食品公司230,000多名顾客开展的随机田野实验。碳足迹标签仅使平均排放降低了0.6%，并且在反对环境助推（nudge）的顾客中适得其反，这些顾客的膳食排放反而增加。尽管环境影响有限，这些标签仍为我们的合作企业带来了正向财务回报，使顾客留存率提高了1.0%，平均每位顾客每周利润提高了0.9%。因此，尽管气候标签很可能仍将是受欢迎的可持续性助推手段，但其环境效益很小，并可能在两极分化的环境中适得其反。

title: Reaching Across the Aisle: Polarization and Grassroots Climate Mobilization
The Narrative of Policy Change: Effects on Policy Preferences, Political Efficacy, and Contributions to Climate Action
abstract: Policy progress often advances incrementally, and citizen movements must sustain engagement across wins and losses. Wins could mobilize citizens by building political-efficacy beliefs—perceived government responsiveness to citizen demands—but could also deflate demand for additional policy. In an online experiment (N=6,000), learning about a major US climate policy slightly increases political-efficacy beliefs, but reduces demand for additional policy and has no effect on climate advocacy. In contrast, combining this information with a fictional story linking legislation to citizen action increases political-efficacy beliefs, policy demand, information-gathering about climate marches, and lobbying donations. Storytelling may therefore be a powerful way to energize collective action.
abstract_zh: 政策进展往往是渐进的，公民运动必须在胜利与挫折中持续保持参与。胜利可能通过建立政治效能感信念（即公众对政府回应民众诉求的感知）来动员公民，但也可能削弱对进一步政策的需求。在一项在线实验（N=6,000）中，了解一项重要的美国气候政策会略微提高政治效能感信念，但会降低对进一步政策的需求，并且对气候倡导没有影响。相比之下，将这一信息与一个将立法与公民行动联系起来的虚构故事相结合，则会提高政治效能感信念、政策需求、对气候游行信息的搜寻以及游说捐款。因此，讲故事或许是激发集体行动的一种有力方式。

title: Ending Global Poverty: Why Money Isn't Enough
